input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 (p0026) runs against us: it is a Customer-side most-favoured-nation/matching obligation requiring us to disclose to Vendor, and match for Vendor, any more favourable commercial offer we receive before engaging another provider. It is open-ended — no defined product, no time limit and no like-for-like comparison carve-outs — so it fails every fallback element and sits in walk-away territory (open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor). No Vendor-granted MFN in our favour exists anywhere in the document, so nothing beneficial is disturbed; § 12.3 (p0044) in fact records that "Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment", which § 7.2 directly contradicts. We therefore take the preferred position and replace the obligation with a statement that we owe Vendor no MFN, offering the defined-product/12-month/like-for-like fallback in the comment if Vendor needs protection.

proposal.summary: Replace § 7.2's Customer-side disclose-and-match obligation with an express statement that Customer owes Vendor no MFN.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the § 7.2 requirement that we disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor and confirmed instead that we owe Vendor no most-favoured-nation obligation; our playbook accepts MFN pricing only in our favour, and § 12.3 already records that we made no most-favoured-customer commitment. If Vendor needs some protection, we could discuss an MFN limited to one defined product for 12 months with like-for-like comparison carve-outs.

ops.oldText: Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
ops.newText: Customer has no obligation to disclose, match, or extend to Vendor any more favourable commercial offer or terms available to a third party.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
